Neon's free plan limits are 100 CU-hours of compute per project per month and per-project storage. The storage figure conflicts across sources, so check the current docs before relying on it.

- **Compute:** Free projects get 100 CU-hours per month, with autoscaling up to 2 CU (≈8 GB RAM). Compute suspends when a monthly limit is reached (compute suspends when monthly limits are reached), and suspended computes don't accrue CU-hours (Suspended computes do not accrue CU-hours.).

The pricing page may be out of date, so verify on neon.com/docs before relying on either number.
- **Other limits:** Free projects can have 10 branches per project. Free plan egress is 5 GB per month. Scale-to-zero occurs after 5 minutes of inactivity, so idle databases use no compute-hours.
- **Plan count:** The free plan allows 100 projects.
- **Upgrade path:** Launch is pay-as-you-go at $0.106/CU-hour plus $0.35/GB-month for storage.

I couldn't open any of the pricing pages directly (the fetch tool was blocked), so these figures come from search-result summaries. Several sources disagree, and the conflicts are marked below. Check the official pages before you rely on a number.

| | **Neon** | **Supabase** | **PlanetScale** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free Postgres tier? | Yes | Yes | **No** |
| Database storage | 0.5 GB per project on the pricing page, or 1 GB per project per a later Neon blog post (conflict) | 500 MB per project | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month, autoscaling up to 2 CU | Not found in the results | n/a |
| Idle behavior | Scales to zero after 5 minutes idle, and suspended computes don't use CU-hours | Projects pause after 1 week of inactivity | n/a |
| Project limit | 100 projects, 10 branches per project | 2 active projects | n/a |
| Egress | 5 GB per month | 5 GB, but one source says 500 MB (conflict) | n/a |
| Extras | None found | 50,000 monthly active users; file storage of 1 GB on the official page or 500 MB per another source (conflict) | n/a |
| Cheapest paid option | Pay-as-you-go: $0.106 per CU-hour plus $0.35 per GB-month | Pro at $25/month, which removes the pause | Base at $5/month, a single-node PS-5 (1/16 vCPU, 512 MB); 3-node HA clusters from $15/month |

**PlanetScale:** The sources say it dropped its free Hobby plan in April 2024 and hasn't brought it back. Some CostBench pages claim a "forever free plan" as of June 2026, but other pages on that same site say there is no free tier, so I'd discount those claims.

**Takeaways:**
- **Neon:** Its free plan has the most generous compute, and it scales to zero when idle.
- **Supabase:** It offers a bundled backend (auth and file storage). The cost is the pause after a week of inactivity and the cap of two projects.
- **PlanetScale:** It has no free tier, so the cheapest way in is the $5/month Base plan.
